title: Kana Explorer Checkpoint
concept: Pre-A1 hiragana, katakana, sound tools, reading, and IME input

questions.prompt: Place the five basic vowel hiragana in standard Japanese order.
questions.explanation: The vowel order あ・い・う・え・お organizes both kana charts.

questions.prompt: Which katakana word represents koohii, coffee?
questions.explanation: Katakana commonly writes loanwords, and ー lengthens the preceding vowel.

questions.prompt: Which learner romaji matches がっこう?
questions.explanation: Small っ doubles the following consonant: がっこう becomes gakkou.

questions.prompt: Which IME keys produce the spelling こんばんは?
questions.explanation: The final topic particle is pronounced wa but spelled は, so an IME needs konbanha.

questions.prompt: When you hear one beat per kana in さかな, which rhythm should you tap?
questions.explanation: Japanese rhythm is organized in morae: さ・か・な has three roughly even beats.

options.label: さ・か・な — three even beats
さか・な — two stressed beats

questions.prompt: A classmate asks how to type the written kana へ when it is a particle. What is the useful answer?
questions.explanation: The particle is pronounced e, but IME spelling follows the visible kana へ, so type he.

options.label: It sounds like e, but type he for へ.
It is always written え, so type e.
Type we because it is a direction.
